title: Mesh cleanup: hole fill, ceiling cap, floater removal
summary: First scene-graph stage: clean the reconstruction mesh into a watertight collision mesh suitable for traversal.

acceptance_tests.test: Given a corpus reconstruction, the service outputs a cleaned collision mesh with holes filled, the ceiling capped, and floaters removed.
Unit tests cover hole fill, cap, and floater removal on synthetic meshes.
requirements.txt pins exact versions; pip-audit clean.

history.event: Builder (AUTH #027, gj-scenegraph hat): built services/scenegraph/ — the traversal-quality mesh-cleanup stage. Pure standard library (no Open3D/numpy): parses the reconstruction collision OBJ, removes disconnected floaters (vertex union-find components; the largest is always kept), fills small holes and caps the open ceiling (boundary-loop fan fill; large side openings are left as doorways unless --fill-all-holes), and reports watertightness + per-step stats. Files: scenegraph/mesh.py (Mesh + OBJ read/write + edge/boundary helpers), scenegraph/cleanup.py (CleanupConfig + clean_mesh + floater/hole/ceiling ops), scenegraph/cli.py, tests (11 pass: floater / small-hole / ceiling-cap / large-side-opening / watertight / degenerate / OBJ round-trip / face-format), requirements.txt (stdlib-only), README. ruff + format + pytest green. AT-2 (synthetic-mesh unit tests) and AT-3 (deps pinned; pure stdlib -> pip-audit trivially clean) met. AT-1 (before/after renders on 3 corpus rooms) rides the Operator's reconstruction runs on the corpus (needs the corpus scans + GPU). Status open -> in-progress.
